title: Noetherian regular rings are universally catenary
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] such that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then $R$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Explicitly, for every finite type commutative $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and every pair of primes $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak b$ of $A$, the lengths of finite strict prime chains between them are bounded by a finite integer, and all saturated chains between them have the same length. A chain is saturated if no prime can be inserted strictly between successive members, and its length is the number of strict inclusions. No finite bound on the dimensions of all local rings of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary, regular-ring consequence using Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM. The hypotheses are Noetherianity and regularity at every prime; the conclusion is universal catenarity, not merely catenarity of R.
